title.zh: 卷九十一 志第四十四 河渠一
title.raw: 卷九十一 志第四十四 河渠一 Volume 91 Treatises 44: Rivers and Canals 1

sentences.zh: 黃河 上

translations.literal: Yellow River — Upper
translations.idiomatic: The Yellow River — Part One

sentences.zh: 黃河自昔為中國患，《河渠書》述之詳矣。

translations.literal: The Yellow River has from ancient times been a calamity for China; the "Rivers and Canals Treatise" describes it in full detail.
translations.idiomatic: From antiquity the Yellow River has been a scourge upon China, and the "Rivers and Canals Treatise" in the Records of the Grand Historian sets forth its history at length.

sentences.zh: 探厥本源，則博望之說，猶為未也。

translations.literal: To probe its ultimate source — even the account of the Marquis of Bowang is still insufficient.
translations.idiomatic: Yet even when one traces it to its ultimate source, the account given by Zhang Qian, Marquis of Bowang, still falls short of the truth.

sentences.zh: 大元至元二十七年，我世祖皇帝命學士蒲察篤實西窮河源，始得其詳。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year of the Yuan reign of the Great Yuan, Our Emperor Shizu commanded the academician Pucha Duoshi to journey west to the utmost source of the river, and for the first time its full particulars were obtained.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-seventh year of the Zhiyuan era (1290), during the Great Yuan, Our Emperor Shizu ordered the academician Pucha Duoshi to travel west to the furthest source of the river, and only then were its true details ascertained.

sentences.zh: 今西蕃朵甘思南鄙曰星宿海者，其源也，四山之間，有泉近百泓，匯而為海，登高望之，若星宿布列，故名。

translations.literal: Today on the southern border of Duo Gan Si in the Western Territories there is a place called the Sea of Starry Constellations — this is its source. Between four mountains there are nearly a hundred springs that gather into a sea; viewed from a height, they appear like stars arrayed in the sky, hence the name.
translations.idiomatic: Its source lies today on the southern frontier of Duo Gan Si in the Western Territories, at a place called the Sea of Starry Constellations. Between four mountains nearly a hundred springs pool into a lake; from the heights they look like stars strewn across the sky, and so it was named.

sentences.zh: 流出復瀦，曰哈刺海，東出曰赤賓河，合忽闌、也裏術二河，東北流為九渡河，其水猶清，騎可涉也。

translations.literal: Flowing out, it pools again in what is called Lake Hala; issuing eastward it becomes the Chibin River, joins the Hulan and Yelishu rivers, and flows northeast as the Nine-Crossings River — its waters are still clear, and horsemen can ford it.
translations.idiomatic: The stream flows out and gathers again in Lake Hala. Where it issues eastward it is called the Chibin River; joining the Hulan and Yelishu rivers, it runs northeast as the Nine-Crossings River, its waters still clear enough for horsemen to wade across.

sentences.zh: 貫山中行，出西戎之都會，曰闊即、曰闊提者，合納憐河，所謂「細黃河」也，水流已濁。

translations.literal: It runs through the mountains, emerges at the capital of the Western Rong — called Kuoji or Kuoti — joins the Naling River, the so-called "slender Yellow River," and by then its waters are already turbid.
translations.idiomatic: Threading through the mountains, it emerges at the western capital called Kuoji or Kuoti, joins the Naling River — the so-called "slender Yellow River" — and by then the current has already turned muddy.

sentences.zh: 繞昆侖之南，折而東注，合乞裏馬出河，復繞昆侖之北，自貴德、西寧之境，至積石，經河州，過臨洮，合洮河，東北流至蘭州，始入中國。

translations.literal: It circles south of Kunlun, turns and flows east, joins the Qilimachu River, circles north of Kunlun again, passes from the territory of Guide and Xining to Jishi, runs through Hezhou, crosses Lintao, joins the Tao River, flows northeast to Lanzhou, and only then enters China proper.
translations.idiomatic: Winding south of Kunlun, it bends eastward and joins the Qilimachu River, then curves north of Kunlun again. From the lands of Guide and Xining it reaches Jishi, passes Hezhou and Lintao, joins the Tao River, and flows northeast to Lanzhou — where it first enters the Chinese heartland.

sentences.zh: 北繞朔方、北地、上郡而東，經三受降城、豐東勝州，折而南，出龍門，過河中，抵潼關。

translations.literal: It circles north around Shuofang, Beidi, and Shang commanderies and flows east, passes the three Accept-the-Surrender cities and Fengdong Sheng Prefecture, turns south, emerges at Longmen, crosses Hezhong, and reaches Tong Pass.
translations.idiomatic: It sweeps north around Shuofang, Beidi, and Shang commanderies and runs east, passes the three Accept-the-Surrender fortresses and Fengdong Sheng Prefecture, turns south, issues through Longmen, crosses Hezhong, and reaches Tong Pass.

sentences.zh: 東出三門、集津為孟津，過虎牢，而後奔放平壤。

translations.literal: Issuing east through Sanmen and Jijin it becomes the Meng Ford, passes Hulao, and thereafter rushes across the level plain.
translations.idiomatic: Issuing east through Sanmen and Jijin it becomes the Meng Ford, passes Hulao, and then charges out across the flatlands.

sentences.zh: 吞納小水以百數，勢益雄放，無崇山巨磯以防閑之，旁激奔潰，不遵禹跡。

translations.literal: It absorbs hundreds of lesser streams, its force growing ever more mighty and unrestrained; with no lofty mountains or great boulders to restrain it, it surges and bursts aside, no longer following Yu's course.
translations.idiomatic: It swallows hundreds of tributaries, its force growing ever more violent. With no towering mountains or massive reefs to hold it in check, it bursts and spills to the sides, abandoning the course traced by Yu the Great.

sentences.zh: 故虎牢迤東距海口三二千里，恒被其害，宋為特甚。

translations.literal: Therefore from Hulao eastward to the sea mouth, a distance of two or three thousand li, it has constantly inflicted harm, and under the Song the damage was especially severe.
translations.idiomatic: From Hulao eastward to the sea mouth — two or three thousand li — the region has constantly suffered its ravages, and under the Song the affliction was especially grave.

sentences.zh: 始自滑台、大伾，嘗兩經泛溢，復禹跡矣。

translations.literal: Beginning from Huatai and Dapi, it twice overflowed its banks and returned to Yu's course.
translations.idiomatic: Beginning at Huatai and Dapi, it twice broke its banks in catastrophic floods and returned to the course laid down by Yu.

sentences.zh: 一時奸臣建議，必欲回之，俾復故流，竭天下之力以塞之。

translations.literal: At one time treacherous ministers proposed that it must be turned back to restore its old channel, exhausting the empire's strength to block it.
translations.idiomatic: At one point treacherous ministers insisted that the river must be forced back into its former channel, and the empire exhausted its resources trying to dam it.

sentences.zh: 屢塞屢決，至南渡而後，貽其禍于金源氏，由不能順其就下之性以導之故也。

translations.literal: It was blocked again and again and burst again and again; after the southward crossing of the dynasty, the calamity was bequeathed to the Jin of the Golden Source, because they could not comply with its nature of seeking the lower ground and guide it accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Time after time it was dammed and time after time it broke through. After the court crossed south, the disaster was passed on to the Jin of the Golden Source — all because no one would yield to the river's nature of seeking lower ground and channel it accordingly.

sentences.zh: 若江，若淮，若洛、汴、衡漳，暨江、淮以南諸水，皆有舟楫溉灌之利者，曆敘其事而分紀之。

translations.literal: As for the Yangtze, the Huai, the Luo, Bian, Heng, and Zhang rivers, together with all waters south of the Yangtze and Huai that afford the benefits of shipping and irrigation — their affairs are narrated in sequence and recorded in separate sections.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangtze, the Huai, the Luo, Bian, Heng, and Zhang rivers, and all the waters south of the Yangtze and Huai that serve shipping and irrigation — each is treated in turn and recorded in its own section.

sentences.zh: 為《河渠志》。

translations.literal: This constitutes the "Rivers and Canals Treatise."
translations.idiomatic: These form the "Rivers and Canals Treatise."

sentences.zh: 河入中國，行太行西，曲折山間，不能為大患。

translations.literal: After the river enters China proper, it runs west of the Taihang Mountains, winding through the hills, and cannot become a great calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Once the river enters the Chinese heartland it runs west of the Taihang range, twisting through the mountains, and cannot yet do great harm.

sentences.zh: 既出大岯，東走赴海，更平地二千餘里，禹跡既湮，河並為一，特以堤防為之限。

translations.literal: After emerging from Dapi, it runs east toward the sea across more than two thousand li of level ground; Yu's course having been obliterated, the river has merged into one channel, restrained only by dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Once it clears Dapi and races east toward the sea across more than two thousand li of flat country, Yu's ancient course long buried, the waters have merged into a single stream held in only by embankments.

sentences.zh: 夏秋霖潦，百川眾流所會，不免決溢之憂，然有司所以備河者，亦益工矣。

translations.literal: In summer and autumn, when seasonal rains and floods gather the waters of a hundred rivers, the fear of breaches and overflows cannot be avoided; yet the measures taken by officials to guard against the river grew ever more skilled as well.
translations.idiomatic: In summer and autumn the seasonal rains gather a hundred rivers into one torrent, and the threat of breach and flood is never far off — yet the officials charged with river defense grew ever more adept at their work.

sentences.zh: 自周顯德初，大決東平之楊劉，宰相李谷監治堤，自陽谷抵張秋口以遏之，水患少息。

translations.literal: From the beginning of the Xiande reign of Zhou, a great breach occurred at Yangliu in Dongping; the chief minister Li Gu supervised dike repairs from Yanggu to Zhangqiukou to check the flood, and the water calamity subsided somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: From the opening years of Later Zhou's Xiande reign, the river burst catastrophically at Yangliu in Dongping. Chief Minister Li Gu oversaw dike repairs from Yanggu to Zhangqiukou to hold the flood back, and the waters eased somewhat.

sentences.zh: 然決河不復故道，離而為赤河。

translations.literal: Yet the breached river did not return to its old course but split off as the Red River.
translations.idiomatic: But the broken channel never rejoined the old course; it split away as the Red River.

sentences.zh: 太祖乾德二年，遣使案行，將治古堤。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Qiande reign of Emperor Taizu, envoys were dispatched to survey the route, intending to repair the ancient dikes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Taizu's Qiande reign (964), envoys were sent to survey the river with plans to restore the ancient dikes.

sentences.zh: 議者以舊河不可卒復，力役且大，遂止。

translations.literal: Counselors held that the old channel could not be swiftly restored and that the labor levy would be enormous, so the project was halted.
translations.idiomatic: Advisers argued that the old channel could not be restored quickly and that the labor required would be enormous, and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 但詔民治遙堤，以禦沖注之患。

translations.literal: Only an edict was issued ordering the people to repair the distant dikes to guard against the peril of direct assault by the current.
translations.idiomatic: The court merely ordered the populace to maintain the outer dikes as a buffer against the river's direct onslaught.

sentences.zh: 其後赤河決東平之竹村，七州之地復罹水災。

translations.literal: Thereafter the Red River breached at Zhucun in Dongping, and the territory of seven prefectures again suffered flood disaster.
translations.idiomatic: Later the Red River broke through at Zhucun in Dongping, and seven prefectures were inundated once more.

sentences.zh: 三年秋，大雨霖，開封府河決陽武，又孟州水漲，壞中氵單橋樑，澶、鄆亦言河決，詔發州兵治之。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the third year, prolonged heavy rains caused the river to breach at Yangwu in Kaifeng prefecture; the waters of Mengzhou also rose and destroyed the Zhongtan Bridge; Chan and Yun prefectures also reported breaches, and an edict ordered prefectural troops dispatched to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn brought weeks of torrential rain. The river broke at Yangwu in Kaifeng prefecture; floods in Mengzhou destroyed the Zhongtan Bridge; Chan and Yun also reported breaches. An edict mobilized troops from the affected prefectures to make repairs.

sentences.zh: 四年八月，滑州河決，壞靈河縣大堤，詔殿前都指揮使韓重贇、馬步軍都軍頭王廷義等督士卒丁夫數萬人治之，被泛者蠲其秋租。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the fourth year, the river breached at Huazhou and destroyed the great dike of Linghe County; an edict ordered the Palace Front commander-in-chief Han Chongyun, the cavalry and infantry commander Wang Tingyi, and others to supervise tens of thousands of soldiers and laborers in repairs; those inundated were exempted from the autumn land tax.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the fourth year the river broke at Huazhou and destroyed Linghe County's main embankment. Taizu ordered Palace Front commander Han Chongyun, cavalry and infantry commander Wang Tingyi, and others to direct tens of thousands of soldiers and conscript laborers in the repair work, and exempted flood victims from the autumn land tax.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，帝以河堤屢決，分遣使行視，發畿甸丁夫繕治。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, because the river dikes had repeatedly breached, the Emperor dispatched envoys in separate parties to inspect the works and mobilized laborers from the capital region to repair them.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year, with the dikes breaking again and again, the Emperor sent out multiple inspection teams and mobilized conscript labor from the capital districts for repairs.

sentences.zh: 自是歲以為常，皆以正月首事，季春而畢。

translations.literal: Thereafter this became an annual routine: work always began in the first month and was completed by late spring.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter this became annual routine — work always began in the first month and wrapped up by late spring.

sentences.zh: 是月，詔開封大名府、鄆澶滑孟濮齊淄滄棣濱德博懷衛鄭等州長吏，並兼本州河堤使，蓋以謹力役而重水患也。

translations.literal: That month an edict ordered the chief officials of Kaifeng, Daming, Yun, Chan, Hua, Meng, Pu, Qi, Zi, Cang, Di, Bin, De, Bo, Huai, Wei, Zheng, and other prefectures each to hold concurrently the post of river-dike commissioner for their prefecture — so that corvée labor might be strictly managed and flood peril taken seriously.
translations.idiomatic: That same month an edict required the chief officials of Kaifeng, Daming, Yun, Chan, Hua, Meng, Pu, Qi, Zi, Cang, Di, Bin, De, Bo, Huai, Wei, Zheng, and other riverine prefectures to serve concurrently as their prefecture's river-dike commissioner — tightening control over corvée labor and underscoring the gravity of flood control.

sentences.zh: 開寶四年十一月，河決澶淵，泛數州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the fourth year of Kaibao, the river breached at Chanyuan and inundated several prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of Kaibao 4 (971), the river broke at Chanyuan and flooded several prefectures.

sentences.zh: 官守不時上言，通判、司封郎中姚恕棄市，知州杜審肇坐免。

translations.literal: The officials on duty had not reported in timely fashion; the vice-prefect and Secretariat Master of Records Yao Shu was executed in the marketplace, and the prefect Du Shenzhao was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Local officials had failed to report promptly. Vice-prefect Yao Shu, Secretariat Master of Records, was executed in the marketplace, and Prefect Du Shenzhao was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，詔曰：「應緣黃、汴、清、禦等河州縣，除准舊制種藝桑棗外，委長吏課民別樹榆柳及土地所宜之木。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, an edict stated: "In all prefectures and counties along the Yellow, Bian, Qing, and Yu rivers, apart from planting mulberry and jujube as permitted under the old regulations, chief officials are charged to require the people additionally to plant elm, willow, and trees suited to the local soil."
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year an edict declared: "Along the Yellow, Bian, Qing, and Yu rivers, beyond the mulberry and jujube already required by statute, local officials shall compel the people to plant elm, willow, and whatever trees suit the soil."

sentences.zh: 仍案戶籍高下，定為五等：第一等歲樹五十本，第二等以下遞減十本。

translations.literal: Household registers were still to be consulted for rank, divided into five grades: the first grade was to plant fifty trees per year, and each grade below was to plant ten fewer.
translations.idiomatic: Households were ranked in five grades by wealth: the top grade planted fifty trees a year, each lower grade ten fewer.

sentences.zh: 民欲廣樹藝者聽，其孤、寡、煢、獨者免。

translations.literal: Those among the people who wished to plant more widely were permitted to do so; orphans, widows, the childless, and the solitary were exempted.
translations.idiomatic: Those who wished to plant more than required were free to do so; orphans, widows, the childless, and the utterly alone were exempt.

sentences.zh: 是月，澶州修河卒賜以錢、鞋，役夫給以茶。

translations.literal: That month, soldiers repairing the river at Chanzhou were given money and shoes, and corvée laborers were provided tea.
translations.idiomatic: That month soldiers working the dikes at Chanzhou received cash and shoes, and conscript laborers were given tea.

sentences.zh: 三月，詔曰：「朕每念河渠潰決，頗為民患，故署使職以總領焉，宜委官聯佐治其事。

translations.literal: In the third month, an edict stated: "We constantly reflect that breaches of rivers and canals are a considerable affliction upon the people; therefore commissioner posts have been established to oversee the work in general, and officials should be delegated in concert to assist in governing these affairs."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month an edict read: "We are ever mindful that river and canal breaches bring great suffering to the people. Commissioner posts have been created to oversee the work, and officials at every level should be assigned to assist."

sentences.zh: 自今開封等十七州府，各置河堤判官一員，以本州通判充；

translations.literal: From now on, in the seventeen prefectures including Kaifeng, one river-dike judicial officer is to be appointed in each, filled by that prefecture's vice-prefect;
translations.idiomatic: Henceforth each of the seventeen prefectures including Kaifeng shall appoint one river-dike judicial officer, to be filled by the prefecture's vice-prefect;

sentences.zh: 如通判闕員，即以本州判官充。

translations.literal: if the vice-prefect post is vacant, the prefectural judicial officer shall fill it.
translations.idiomatic: and if the vice-prefect post is vacant, the prefectural judicial officer shall serve instead.

sentences.zh: 」五月，河大決濮陽，又決陽武。

translations.literal: In the fifth month the river burst catastrophically at Puyang and again at Yangwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the river broke catastrophically at Puyang and again at Yangwu.

sentences.zh: 詔發諸州兵及丁夫凡五萬人，遣潁州團練使曹翰護其役。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized troops and corvée labor from the various prefectures totaling fifty thousand men, and dispatched Yingzhou regiment commander Cao Han to oversee the work.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized fifty thousand troops and conscript laborers from the affected prefectures and sent Yingzhou regiment commander Cao Han to supervise the repairs.

sentences.zh: 翰辭，太祖謂曰：「霖雨不止，又聞河決。

translations.literal: Han declined; Taizu said to him: "The seasonal rains have not ceased, and we have again heard of a river breach.
translations.idiomatic: Han tried to decline. Taizu told him: "The rains have not stopped, and we have word of another breach.

sentences.zh: 朕信宿以來，焚香上禱於天，若天災流行，願在朕躬，勿延於民也。

translations.literal: For two nights now We have burned incense and prayed Heaven above: if heavenly calamity must spread, let it fall upon Our person and not extend to the people."
translations.idiomatic: For two nights I have burned incense and prayed to Heaven: if disaster must come, let it strike me alone and not reach the people."

sentences.zh: 翰頓首對曰：「昔宋景公諸侯耳，一發善言，災星退舍。

translations.literal: Han bowed his head and replied: "In former times Duke Jing of Song was but a feudal lord, yet a single utterance of good words made the calamitous star withdraw from its lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Han kowtowed and answered: "Duke Jing of Song was only a feudal lord, yet a single word of compassion made the disaster star retreat from its station.

sentences.zh: 今陛下憂及兆庶，懇禱如是，固當上感天心，必不為災。」

translations.literal: Now Your Majesty's concern reaches the myriad masses, and Your earnest prayer is such as this — surely it will move Heaven's heart on high, and calamity will certainly not come."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty's concern reaches every soul under Heaven, and your prayer is so earnest — surely Heaven will be moved, and disaster will not come."

sentences.zh: 六月，下詔曰：「近者澶、濮等數州，霖雨薦降，洪河為患。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, an edict was issued stating: "Recently in several prefectures including Chan and Pu, seasonal rains have fallen in succession and the mighty river has become a scourge.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month an edict declared: "In Chan, Pu, and neighboring prefectures the seasonal rains have fallen without cease, and the great river has become a scourge.

sentences.zh: 朕以屢經決溢，重困黎元，每閱前書，詳究經瀆。

translations.literal: We, having repeatedly suffered breaches and overflows that heavily afflict the common people, each time consult the ancient books and thoroughly investigate the classic waterways.
translations.idiomatic: Repeated breaches and floods have brought heavy suffering to the people. We have turned again and again to the ancient texts, studying every classic account of the waterways.

sentences.zh: 至若夏後所載，但言導河至海，隨山濬川，未聞力制湍流，廣營高岸。

translations.literal: As for what is recorded of the Xia sovereign, it speaks only of guiding the river to the sea and dredging channels along the mountains — nothing is heard of forcibly restraining rushing currents or extensively building high embankments.
translations.idiomatic: What the Xia sovereign's records describe is guiding the river to the sea and dredging channels along the mountains — never forcing raging currents or piling up towering embankments.

sentences.zh: 自戰國專利，堙塞故道，小以妨大，私而害公，九河之制遂隳，歷代之患弗弭。

translations.literal: From the Warring States period onward, when profit was pursued exclusively, old channels were blocked and filled; the lesser obstructed the greater, private interest harmed the public good, the system of the Nine Rivers was thereby destroyed, and the calamities of successive ages were never quelled.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Warring States, when private gain took precedence, old channels were dammed and diverted — the small blocking the great, private interest harming the public good. The system of the Nine Rivers was ruined, and flood disasters persisted through every dynasty.

sentences.zh: 凡搢紳多士、草澤之倫，有素習河渠之書，深知疏導之策，若為經久，可免重勞，並許詣闕上書，附驛條奏。

translations.literal: All gentry scholars and men of the wilds who are versed in books on rivers and canals and deeply understand policies of dredging and guiding — if they have enduring plans that can spare repeated heavy labor — are permitted to come to the court and submit memorials, which may be forwarded by post relay in separate entries.
translations.idiomatic: Any scholar or recluse versed in river engineering who knows how to dredge and channel the waters for a lasting solution — come to court and submit a memorial. Send it by post relay; we will review each proposal in turn.

sentences.zh: 朕當親覽，用其所長，勉副詢求，當示甄獎。

translations.literal: We shall personally review them, employ their strengths, and those who earnestly meet Our inquiry shall receive selection and reward.
translations.idiomatic: We shall read each submission ourselves, employ what is sound, and reward those whose counsel proves worthy.

sentences.zh: 」時東魯逸人田告者，纂《禹元經》十二篇，帝聞之，召至闕下，詢以治水之道，善其言，將授以官，以親老固辭歸養，從之。

translations.literal: " At that time Tian Gao, a recluse of eastern Lu, had compiled twelve chapters of the "Yu Meta-Classic"; when the Emperor heard of it, he summoned him to the palace, inquired of him regarding the Way of controlling water, approved his words, and was about to grant him office — but Tian firmly declined on grounds that his parents were elderly and wished to return home to support them; the Emperor acceded.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time Tian Gao, a recluse from eastern Lu, had compiled twelve chapters of the "Yu Meta-Classic." The Emperor heard of it, summoned him to court, and questioned him on flood control. Impressed by his counsel, Taizu was about to offer him office — but Tian pleaded that his parents were elderly and he must return home to care for them. The Emperor let him go.

sentences.zh: 翰至河上，親督工徒，未幾，決河皆塞。

translations.literal: Han reached the river and personally supervised the workers; before long, all the breached sections were blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Han reached the river and personally directed the labor crews. Before long every breach was sealed.

sentences.zh: 太宗太平興國二年秋七月，河決孟州之溫縣、鄭州之滎澤、澶州之頓丘，皆發緣河諸州丁夫塞之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of autumn in the second year of Taiping Xingguo of Emperor Taizong, the river breached at Wen County in Mengzhou, Xingze in Zhengzhou, and Dunqiu in Chanzhou; corvée labor was mobilized from all riverine prefectures to block the breaches.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of Taizong's second Taiping Xingguo year (977), the river broke at Wen County in Mengzhou, Xingze in Zhengzhou, and Dunqiu in Chanzhou. Conscript labor from every riverine prefecture was mobilized to seal the breaches.

sentences.zh: 又遣左衛大將軍李崇矩騎置自陝西至滄、棣，案行水勢。

translations.literal: The Left Guard grand general Li Chongju was also dispatched with relay horses from west of Shan to Cang and Di to survey the water conditions.
translations.idiomatic: Left Guard grand general Li Chongju was also sent with relay horses from west of Shan to Cang and Di to survey conditions along the river.

sentences.zh: 視堤岸之缺，亟繕治之；

translations.literal: Wherever dikes and banks showed gaps, he hastened to repair them;
translations.idiomatic: Wherever the dikes showed gaps he ordered immediate repairs;

sentences.zh: 民被水災者，悉蠲其租。

translations.literal: for the people who had suffered flood disaster, all land rents were remitted.
translations.idiomatic: and all land tax was remitted for flood victims.

sentences.zh: 三年正月，命使十七人分治黃河堤，以備水患。

translations.literal: In the first month of the third year, seventeen envoys were appointed to administer the Yellow River dikes in separate jurisdictions as a precaution against flood peril.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the third year seventeen envoys were appointed, each responsible for a section of the Yellow River dikes.

sentences.zh: 滑州靈河縣河塞復決，命西上閣門使郭守文率卒塞之。

translations.literal: At Linghe County in Huazhou, where the river had been blocked, it breached again; the Western Upper Gate envoy Guo Shouwen was ordered to lead troops to seal it.
translations.idiomatic: At Linghe County in Huazhou a previously sealed breach opened again. Western Upper Gate envoy Guo Shouwen was ordered to lead troops to close it.

sentences.zh: 七年，河大漲，蹙清河，淩鄆州，城將陷，塞其門，急奏以聞。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the river rose greatly, pressed upon the Qing River, and threatened Yunzhou; the city was about to fall, its gates were blocked, and urgent memorials were sent to report.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the river swelled enormously, pressing the Qing River and threatening Yunzhou. With the city about to be engulfed, its gates were sealed and urgent dispatches sent to court.

sentences.zh: 詔殿前承旨劉吉馳往固之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the Palace Front recipient Liu Ji to ride posthaste to strengthen the defenses.
translations.idiomatic: An edict sent Palace Front recipient Liu Ji galloping to reinforce the defenses.

sentences.zh: 八年五月，河大決滑州韓村，泛澶、濮、曹、濟諸州民田，壞居人廬舍，東南流至彭城界入於淮。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the eighth year, the river burst catastrophically at Hancun in Huazhou, inundated the civilian fields of Chan, Pu, Cao, and Ji prefectures, destroyed dwellings, and flowed southeast to the border of Pengcheng, entering the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of the eighth year the river broke catastrophically at Hancun in Huazhou, flooding farmland across Chan, Pu, Cao, and Ji, destroying homes, and running southeast to the Pengcheng border where it entered the Huai.

sentences.zh: 詔發丁夫塞之。

translations.literal: An edict mobilized corvée labor to block it.
translations.idiomatic: An edict mobilized conscript labor to seal the breach.

sentences.zh: 堤久不成，乃命使者按視遙堤舊址。

translations.literal: The dikes long remained unfinished, so envoys were ordered to survey the sites of the old distant dikes.
translations.idiomatic: The dikes remained unfinished for a long time, so envoys were sent to survey the sites of the old outer embankments.

sentences.zh: 使回條奏，以為「治遙堤不如分水勢。

translations.literal: When the envoys returned they submitted separate memorials, holding that "repairing distant dikes is inferior to dividing the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: On their return the envoys submitted separate memorials arguing that "repairing outer dikes is less effective than splitting the river's force.

sentences.zh: 自孟抵鄆，雖有堤防，唯滑與澶最為隘狹。

translations.literal: From Meng to Yun, although there are dikes, only Hua and Chan are most narrow and constricted.
translations.idiomatic: From Meng to Yun there are dikes throughout, but the channel is narrowest at Hua and Chan.

sentences.zh: 於此二州之地，可立分水之制，宜於南北岸各開其一，北入王莽河以通于海，南入靈河以通於淮，節減暴流，一如汴口之法。

translations.literal: In the territory of these two prefectures, a system of dividing the waters may be established: it is fitting to open one channel on each of the north and south banks — northward into the Wang Mang River to reach the sea, southward into the Ling River to reach the Huai — moderating the violent current, just as at the Bian River mouth.
translations.idiomatic: At these two prefectures a water-diversion system should be built: open one channel on each bank — north into the Wang Mang River to reach the sea, south into the Ling River to reach the Huai — to tame the raging current, just as at the Bian River mouth.

sentences.zh: 其分水河，量其遠邇，作為斗門，啟閉隨時，務乎均濟。

translations.literal: For these diversion channels, measuring their distance, sluice gates should be constructed, opened and closed according to the season, striving for balanced distribution.
translations.idiomatic: Along each diversion channel, sluice gates should be built at measured intervals, opened and closed as conditions require, to keep the flow evenly distributed.

sentences.zh: 通舟運，溉農田，此富庶之資也。

translations.literal: Opening shipping and irrigating farmland — these are resources for prosperity.
translations.idiomatic: Shipping and irrigation would follow — the foundations of prosperity.

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: No response was given.
translations.idiomatic: The court gave no response.

sentences.zh: 時多陰雨，河久未塞，帝憂之，遣樞密直學士張齊賢乘傳詣白馬津，用太牢加璧以祭。

translations.literal: At that time there was much overcast rain; the river long remained unblocked, and the Emperor was troubled; he dispatched Privy Council academician Zhang Qixian by relay to the White Horse Ford to offer sacrifice with a great victim and jade disc.
translations.idiomatic: Rain fell for weeks on end and the breach would not close. Troubled, the Emperor sent Privy Council academician Zhang Qixian by relay to the White Horse Ford to offer sacrifice with a great victim and jade disc.

sentences.zh: 十二月，滑州言決河塞，群臣稱賀。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, Huazhou reported that the breached river had been blocked, and the assembled ministers offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month Huazhou reported the breach sealed, and the court celebrated.

sentences.zh: 九年春，滑州復言房村河決，帝曰：「近以河決韓村，發民治堤不成，安可重困吾民，當以諸軍代之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the ninth year, Huazhou again reported a breach at Fangcun; the Emperor said: "Recently when the river breached at Hancun, mobilizing the people to repair the dikes did not succeed — how can We again heavily afflict Our people? The various armies should replace them."
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the ninth year Huazhou reported another breach at Fangcun. The Emperor said: "When the river broke at Hancun we mobilized civilians to repair the dikes and failed. How can we burden the people again? Send the armies instead."

sentences.zh: 」乃發卒五萬，以侍衛步軍都指揮使田重進領其役，又命翰林學士宋白祭白馬津，沈乙太牢加璧，未幾役成。

translations.literal: Fifty thousand troops were then mobilized, with Palace Guard infantry commander Tian Zhongjin leading the work; the Hanlin academician Song Bai was also ordered to sacrifice at the White Horse Ford, casting the yi vessel with a great victim and jade disc; before long the labor was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Fifty thousand troops were mobilized under Palace Guard infantry commander Tian Zhongjin. Hanlin academician Song Bai was again sent to sacrifice at the White Horse Ford, casting the yi vessel with a great victim and jade disc. Before long the work was done.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年三月，詔：「長吏以下及巡河主埽使臣，經度行視河堤，勿致壞隳，違者當寘於法。

translations.literal: In the third month of the second year of Chunhua, an edict stated: "Chief officials and below, together with river-patrol chief-bund commissioner envoys, are to survey and inspect the river dikes on circuit and must not allow damage or collapse; violators shall be punished according to law."
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Chunhua 2 (991) an edict ordered: "Chief officials and river-patrol commissioners must inspect the dikes regularly and prevent damage or collapse. Violators will be punished by law."

sentences.zh: 」四年十月，河決澶州，陷北城，壞廬舍七千余區，詔發卒代民治之。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the fourth year, the river breached at Chanzhou, the north city fell, more than seven thousand dwellings were destroyed, and an edict mobilized troops to replace the people in repairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the fourth year the river broke at Chanzhou, the north city was inundated, and more than seven thousand homes were destroyed. An edict sent troops to do the repair work in place of civilians.

sentences.zh: 是歲，巡河供奉官梁睿上言：「滑州土脈疏，岸善隤，每歲河決南岸，害民田。

translations.literal: That year, river-patrol tribute official Liang Rui submitted a memorial: "The soil at Huazhou is loose, the banks readily collapse, and every year the river breaches on the south bank, harming the people's fields.
translations.idiomatic: That year river-patrol tribute official Liang Rui memorialized: "The soil at Huazhou is loose and the banks crumble easily. Every year the river breaks on the south bank and destroys farmland.

sentences.zh: 請于迎陽鑿渠引水，凡四十里，至黎陽合大河，以防暴漲。

translations.literal: We request that a channel be cut at Yingyang to draw off water, forty li in all, reaching Liyang where it joins the great river, to guard against sudden floods."
translations.idiomatic: I propose cutting a diversion channel at Yingyang, forty li long, to join the main river at Liyang and relieve sudden floods."

sentences.zh: 」帝許之。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved it.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，滑州言新渠成，帝又案圖，命昭宣使羅州刺史杜彥鈞率兵夫，計功十七萬，鑿河開渠，自韓村埽至州西鐵狗廟，凡十五余裏，復合於河，以分水勢。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Huazhou reported that the new channel was completed; the Emperor again consulted maps and ordered the Zhaoxuan envoy and Luozhou prefect Du Yanjun to lead soldiers and laborers, reckoning the work at one hundred seventy thousand units, to cut the river and open a channel from the Hancun bund to the Iron Dog Temple west of the prefecture — more than fifteen li in all — rejoining the river to divide the water's force.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Huazhou reported the new channel complete. The Emperor studied the maps and ordered Zhaoxuan envoy and Luozhou prefect Du Yanjun to lead soldiers and laborers — reckoned at 170,000 work units — to cut a channel from the Hancun bund to the Iron Dog Temple west of the city, more than fifteen li, rejoining the main river to split the current.

sentences.zh: 真宗咸平三年五月，河決鄆州王陵埽，浮钜野，入淮、泗，水勢悍激，侵迫州城。

translations.literal: In the fifth month of the third year of Xianping of Emperor Zhenzong, the river breached at the Wangling bund in Yunzhou, floated across Juye, entered the Huai and Si, its current fierce and violent, pressing upon the prefectural city.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month of Zhenzong's third Xianping year (1000) the river broke at the Wangling bund in Yunzhou, spread across Juye, and poured into the Huai and Si with such force that it threatened the prefectural city.

sentences.zh: 命使率諸州丁男二萬人塞之，逾月而畢。

translations.literal: Envoys were ordered to lead twenty thousand corvée laborers from the various prefectures to block it; after more than a month the work was completed.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys led twenty thousand conscript laborers from the affected prefectures to seal the breach. The work took more than a month.

sentences.zh: 始，赤河決，擁濟、泗，鄆州城中常苦水患。

translations.literal: From the beginning, when the Red River breached, it pressed upon Ji and Si, and within Yunzhou city flood peril was constantly suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since the Red River had broken its banks and pressed upon the Ji and Si, Yunzhou city had lived under constant threat of flood.

sentences.zh: 至是，霖雨彌月，積潦益甚，乃遣工部郎中陳若拙經度徙城。

translations.literal: By this time, seasonal rains had lasted a full month and accumulated floods grew worse; Chen Ruozhuo, director of the Ministry of Works, was dispatched to survey and relocate the city.
translations.idiomatic: Now the rains had lasted a full month and the floods worsened. Ministry of Works director Chen Ruozhuo was sent to survey a site and relocate the city.

sentences.zh: 若拙請徙于東南十五里陽鄉之高原，詔可。

translations.literal: Ruozhuo requested relocation to the high ground of Yangxiang, fifteen li southeast; the edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: Ruozhuo proposed moving to the high ground at Yangxiang, fifteen li southeast. The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 是年，詔：「緣河官吏，雖秩滿，須水落受代。

translations.literal: That year, an edict stated: "Officials along the river, even when their term is complete, must wait until the waters subside before being replaced.
translations.idiomatic: That year an edict declared: "River officials, even when their terms expire, must remain until the waters subside before being replaced.

sentences.zh: 知州、通判兩月一巡堤，縣令、佐迭巡堤防，轉運使勿委以他職。

translations.literal: Prefects and vice-prefects are to inspect the dikes once every two months; magistrates and assistants are to take turns patrolling the embankments; transport commissioners are not to be assigned other duties."
translations.idiomatic: Prefects and vice-prefects shall inspect the dikes every two months; magistrates and assistants shall patrol in rotation; transport commissioners shall not be given other duties."

sentences.zh: 」又申嚴盜伐河上榆柳之禁。

translations.literal: The prohibition against illicit felling of elm and willow along the river was again strictly enforced.
translations.idiomatic: The prohibition on cutting elm and willow along the river was strictly reinforced.

sentences.zh: 著作佐郎李垂上《導河形勝書》三篇並圖，其略曰：

translations.literal: Archives assistant Li Chui submitted three chapters of the "Book on the Terrain Advantages of Guiding the River" together with maps; the summary states:
translations.idiomatic: Archives assistant Li Chui submitted three chapters of the "Book on Guiding the River by Terrain" with maps. The summary reads:

sentences.zh: 臣請自汲郡東推禹故道，挾御河，較其水勢，出大伾、上陽、太行三山之間，復西河故瀆，北注大名西、館陶南，東北合赤河而至於海。

translations.literal: Your subject requests that from east of Ji commandery Yu's old course be traced, flanking the Imperial Canal and comparing water forces, issuing between the three mountains of Dapi, Shangyang, and Taihang, restoring the old channel of the Western River, flowing north to west of Daming and south of Guantao, then northeast joining the Red River to reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: I propose tracing Yu's old course east of Ji commandery, flanking the Imperial Canal and comparing water levels, so the river issues between Dapi, Shangyang, and the Taihang range, restores the Western River's old channel, flows north past west Daming and south Guantao, then northeast joins the Red River to reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 因于魏縣北析一渠，正北稍西逕衡漳直北，下出邢、洺，如《夏書》過洚水，稍東注易水、合百濟、會朝河而至於海。

translations.literal: Then at north Weixian a channel is to be split off, running due north and slightly west through Heng and Zhang straight north, descending to emerge at Xing and Ming — as the "Documents of Xia" says in passing the Jing waters — then slightly east to pour into the Yi River, join the Baiji, meet the Chao River, and reach the sea.
translations.idiomatic: North of Weixian a branch channel would run due north and slightly west through Heng and Zhang, descending to Xing and Ming — as the "Documents of Xia" describes passing the Jing waters — then east to the Yi River, joining the Baiji and Chao rivers to reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 大伾而下，黃、禦混流，薄山障堤，勢不能遠。

translations.literal: Below Dapi, the Yellow and Imperial rivers mingle; pressed by mountains and blocked by dikes, the force cannot extend far.
translations.idiomatic: Below Dapi the Yellow and Imperial rivers mingle; hemmed in by mountains and dikes, the current cannot run far.

sentences.zh: 如是則載之高地而北行，百姓獲利，而契丹不能南侵矣。

translations.literal: If so, bearing it upon high ground northward, the common people would gain benefit, and the Khitan could not invade southward.
translations.idiomatic: Carried on high ground northward, the people would prosper and the Khitan could not invade from the south.

sentences.zh: 《禹貢》所謂「夾右碣石入於海」，孔安國曰：「河逆上此州界。」

translations.literal: What the "Tribute of Yu" calls "passing to the right of Jieshi and entering the sea" — Kong Anguo said: "The river runs counter to the current up to the border of this province."
translations.idiomatic: The "Tribute of Yu" speaks of "passing to the right of Jieshi and entering the sea." Kong Anguo explained: "The river runs upstream against the current to this province's border."

sentences.zh: 其始作自大伾西八十里，曹公所開運渠東五里，引河水正北稍東十里，破伯禹古堤，逕牧馬陂，從禹故道，又東三十里轉大伾西、通利軍北，挾白溝，復西大河，北逕清豐、大名西，曆洹水、魏縣東，暨館陶南，入屯氏故瀆，合赤河而北至於海。

translations.literal: The work is to begin eighty li west of Dapi, five li east of the transport canal opened by Lord Cao; drawing the river due north and slightly east for ten li, breaking through the ancient dike of the Earl of Yu, passing the Horse-Pasturing Marsh, following Yu's old course, then east another thirty li turning west of Dapi and north of Tongli Army, flanking the White Ditch, returning to the great western river, north past west Qingfeng and Daming, along the Huan River and east Weixian, reaching south Guantao, entering the old channel of the Tun clan, joining the Red River and north to the sea.
translations.idiomatic: Work would begin eighty li west of Dapi, five li east of Cao Cao's transport canal: draw the river due north and slightly east for ten li, break through Yu's ancient dike, pass the Horse-Pasturing Marsh along Yu's old course, then thirty li east to west of Dapi and north of Tongli Army, flank the White Ditch, rejoin the western main channel, run north past Qingfeng and west Daming, along the Huan and east Weixian to south Guantao, enter the Tun clan's old channel, join the Red River, and reach the sea.

sentences.zh: 既而自大伾西新發故瀆西岸析一渠，正北稍西五里，廣深與汴等，合御河道，逼大伾北，即堅壤析一渠，東西二十里，廣深與汴等，復東大河。

translations.literal: Then from west of Dapi, on the west bank of the newly opened old channel, a channel is split off due north and slightly west for five li, of width and depth equal to the Bian; joining the Imperial Canal route and pressing north of Dapi, where the soil is firm another channel is split east-west for twenty li, of width and depth equal to the Bian, rejoining the great eastern river.
translations.idiomatic: West of Dapi, on the west bank of the newly opened old channel, a five-li branch would run due north and slightly west, matching the Bian in width and depth, join the Imperial Canal route, and north of Dapi — where the soil is firm — a twenty-li east-west channel of equal dimensions would rejoin the eastern main river.

sentences.zh: 兩渠分流，則三四分水，猶得注澶淵舊渠矣。

translations.literal: With the two channels dividing the flow, three or four parts of the water would be split off, yet the old channel of Chanyuan could still receive its share.
translations.idiomatic: With two diversion channels splitting the flow, three or four parts of the water would be drawn off while the old Chanyuan channel still received its share.

sentences.zh: 大都河水從西大河故瀆東北，合赤河而達於海，然後于魏縣北發御河西岸析一渠，正北稍西六十里，廣深與御河等，合衡漳水；

translations.literal: For the most part the river water would follow the old channel of the great western river northeast, join the Red River, and reach the sea; then at north Weixian, from the west bank of the Imperial Canal, a channel would be split off due north and slightly west for sixty li, of width and depth equal to the Imperial Canal, joining the Heng and Zhang waters;
translations.idiomatic: For the most part the river would follow the western main channel's old course northeast, join the Red River, and reach the sea. Then north of Weixian, from the Imperial Canal's west bank, a sixty-li channel of equal width and depth would run due north and slightly west to join the Heng and Zhang rivers;

sentences.zh: 又冀州北界、深州西南三十里決衡漳西岸，限水為門，西北注滹沱，潦則塞之，使東漸渤海，旱則決之，使西灌屯田，此中國禦邊之利也。

translations.literal: and again at the northern border of Jizhou and thirty li southwest of Shenzhou, the west bank of the Heng and Zhang would be breached, limiting the water with gates; northwest it would pour into the Hutuo — in flood the gates would be closed so it flowed east gradually into the Bohai Sea, in drought they would be opened so it irrigated garrison fields to the west. These are advantages for China's defense of the frontier.
translations.idiomatic: and at Jizhou's northern border, thirty li southwest of Shenzhou, the Heng-Zhang west bank would be gated: northwest into the Hutuo — closed in flood so water flowed east toward the Bohai, opened in drought to irrigate garrison farms to the west. This would strengthen China's frontier defense.

sentences.zh: 兩漢而下，言水利者，屢欲求九河故道而疏之。

translations.literal: From the Two Han dynasties onward, those who spoke of water control repeatedly sought the old courses of the Nine Rivers and dredged them.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han dynasties, hydraulic experts repeatedly sought to reopen and dredge the Nine Rivers' old channels.

sentences.zh: 今考圖志，九河並在平原而北，且河壞澶、滑，未至平原而上已決矣，則九河奚利哉。

translations.literal: Now examining maps and gazetteers, the Nine Rivers all lie north of Pingyuan, yet the river has already breached at Chan and Hua before reaching Pingyuan — what benefit could the Nine Rivers bring?
translations.idiomatic: Maps and gazetteers show the Nine Rivers all lying north of Pingyuan — yet the river already breaks at Chan and Hua before it even reaches that plain. What good would reopening the Nine Rivers do?

sentences.zh: 漢武舍大伾之故道，發頓丘之暴沖，則濫兗泛齊，流患中土，使河朔平田，膏腴千里，縱容邊寇劫掠其間。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Han abandoned the old course at Dapi and released the violent rush at Dunqiu, Yan and Qi were inundated and calamity flowed through the central lands, leaving the level fields of Heshuo — a thousand li of fertile soil — open for frontier raiders to plunder at will.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu abandoned Dapi's old channel and unleashed the violent current at Dunqiu, Yan and Qi were flooded and the heartland suffered — while a thousand li of fertile Heshuo farmland lay open for frontier raiders to plunder.

sentences.zh: 今大河盡東，全燕陷北，而禦邊之計，莫大於河。

translations.literal: Now the great river runs entirely east, all of Yan lies exposed to the north, and among plans for defending the frontier, none is greater than the river.
translations.idiomatic: Today the great river runs entirely east, leaving all of Yan exposed to the north. No frontier defense matters more than controlling the river.

sentences.zh: 不然，則趙、魏百城，富庶萬億，所謂誨盜而招寇矣。

translations.literal: Otherwise, the hundred cities of Zhao and Wei, with their myriad wealth, would be what is called teaching robbers and inviting invaders.
translations.idiomatic: Otherwise the hundred wealthy cities of Zhao and Wei would be — as the saying goes — teaching thieves and inviting raiders.

sentences.zh: 一日伺我饑饉，乘虛入寇，臨時用計者實難；

translations.literal: If one day they watch for Our famine and raid when We are vulnerable, improvising a plan at the last moment would truly be difficult;
translations.idiomatic: If they wait for famine and strike when we are weak, improvised plans at the last moment will not suffice;

sentences.zh: 不如因人足財豐之時，成之為易。

translations.literal: it is better to accomplish the work while manpower is ample and wealth abundant, when completion is easy.
translations.idiomatic: better to complete the work now, while manpower and resources are plentiful.

sentences.zh: 詔樞密直學士任中正、龍圖閣直學士陳彭年、知制誥王曾詳定。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Privy Council academician Ren Zhongzheng, Dragon Diagram Pavilion academician Chen Pengnian, and drafting drafter Wang Zeng to examine and determine the proposal in detail.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commissioned Privy Council academician Ren Zhongzheng, Dragon Diagram Pavilion academician Chen Pengnian, and drafting drafter Wang Zeng to review the proposal.

sentences.zh: 中正等上言：「詳垂所述，頗為周悉。

translations.literal: Zhongzheng and others submitted a memorial: "What Li Chui has set forth in detail is quite comprehensive.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongzheng and his colleagues memorialized: "Li Chui's proposal is thorough and comprehensive.

sentences.zh: 所言起滑台而下，派之為六，則緣流就下，湍急難制，恐水勢聚而為一，不能各依所導。

translations.literal: What he proposes — beginning from Huatai and dividing into six channels — would follow the current downward; the rush would be fierce and hard to control. We fear the water's force would gather into one and could not each follow its intended course.
translations.idiomatic: But dividing the river into six channels from Huatai downward would follow the current's downward rush — fierce and uncontrollable. The waters would likely merge into one torrent rather than follow six separate courses.

sentences.zh: 設或必成六派，則是更增六處河口，悠久難於堤防。

translations.literal: If the six divisions were somehow achieved, this would add six more river mouths, difficult to defend with dikes over the long term.
translations.idiomatic: Even if six channels could be achieved, six additional mouths would be nearly impossible to dike over the long term.

sentences.zh: 亦慮入滹沱、漳河，漸至二水淤塞，益為民患，又築堤七百里，役夫二十一萬七千，工至四十日，侵佔民田，頗為煩費。

translations.literal: We also fear entry into the Hutuo and Zhang rivers, gradually silting both until they become an added affliction upon the people. Moreover, building dikes for seven hundred li, with 217,000 laborers working forty days, would encroach on civilian fields and prove greatly burdensome.
translations.idiomatic: We also fear silting the Hutuo and Zhang until they become a new scourge. Building seven hundred li of dikes would require 217,000 laborers for forty days, seize farmland, and prove enormously costly.

sentences.zh: 」其議遂寢。

translations.literal: The proposal was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was shelved.

sentences.zh: 七年，詔罷葺遙堤，以養民力。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, an edict halted repair of distant dikes to conserve the people's strength.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year an edict halted repair of outer dikes to spare the people's strength.

sentences.zh: 八月，河決澶州大吳埽，役徒數千，築新堤，亙二百四十步，水乃順道。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, the river breached at the Dawu bund in Chanzhou; several thousand workers built a new dike spanning two hundred forty paces, and the water then followed the channel.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month the river broke at the Dawu bund in Chanzhou. Several thousand workers built a new dike two hundred forty paces long, and the water returned to its channel.

sentences.zh: 八年，京西轉運使陳堯佐議開滑州小河分水勢，遣使視利害以聞。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, Jingxi transport commissioner Chen Yaozuo proposed opening a small channel at Huazhou to divide the water's force; envoys were dispatched to survey advantages and disadvantages and report.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year Jingxi transport commissioner Chen Yaozuo proposed opening a small Huazhou channel to split the current. Envoys were sent to survey the pros and cons.

sentences.zh: 及還，請規度自三迎陽村北治之，復開汊河於上游，以泄其壅溢。

translations.literal: On their return they requested planning and measurement from north of Sanyingyang Village, and reopening a branch channel upstream to discharge the congestion and overflow.
translations.idiomatic: On their return they proposed work north of Sanyingyang Village and reopening an upstream branch channel to relieve the backlog.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: The edict approved.
translations.idiomatic: The edict approved.

sentences.zh: 天禧三年六月乙未夜，滑州河溢城西北天臺山旁，俄復潰於城西南，岸摧七百步，漫溢州城，曆澶、濮、曹、鄆，注梁山泊；

translations.literal: On the night of the yiyi day in the sixth month of the third year of Tianxi, the river overflowed at Huazhou beside Tiantai Mountain northwest of the city; soon it breached again southwest of the city, the bank collapsed for seven hundred paces, the flood spread over the prefectural city, passed through Chan, Pu, Cao, and Yun, and poured into Liangshan Marsh;
translations.idiomatic: On the yiyi night of the sixth month of Tianxi 3 (1019), the river overflowed at Huazhou beside Tiantai Mountain northwest of the city, then breached again southwest of the city. Seven hundred paces of bank collapsed, the prefectural city was inundated, and the flood swept through Chan, Pu, Cao, and Yun into Liangshan Marsh;

sentences.zh: 又合清水、古汴渠東入於淮，州邑罹患者三十二。

translations.literal: it then joined the Qing River and the ancient Bian channel flowing east into the Huai; thirty-two prefectures and districts suffered disaster.
translations.idiomatic: then joined the Qing River and ancient Bian channel flowing east into the Huai. Thirty-two prefectures and districts were affected.

sentences.zh: 即遣使賦諸州薪石、楗橛、芟竹之數千六百萬，發兵夫九萬人治之。

translations.literal: Envoys were immediately dispatched to levy from the prefectures sixteen million units of fuel, stone, piles, and reed-bamboo; ninety thousand soldiers and laborers were mobilized for repairs.
translations.idiomatic: Envoys immediately levied sixteen million units of timber, stone, piles, and reed-bamboo from the prefectures and mobilized ninety thousand soldiers and laborers for repairs.

sentences.zh: 四年二月，河塞，群臣入賀，上親為文，刻石紀功。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fourth year, the river was blocked; the assembled ministers entered to offer congratulations, and the Emperor personally composed a text inscribed on stone to record the achievement.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the fourth year the breach was sealed. The court celebrated, and the Emperor personally composed an inscription on stone to commemorate the achievement.

sentences.zh: 是年，祠部員外郎李垂又言疏河利害，命垂至大名府、滑衛德貝州、通利軍與長吏計度。

translations.literal: That year, Sacrifices Bureau vice director Li Chui again spoke on the advantages and disadvantages of dredging the river; Chui was ordered to Daming prefecture, Huazhou, Weizhou, Dezhou, Beizhou, and Tongli Army to plan with the chief officials.
translations.idiomatic: That year Sacrifices Bureau vice director Li Chui again addressed the pros and cons of dredging the river. He was sent to Daming, Huazhou, Weizhou, Dezhou, Beizhou, and Tongli Army to consult with local officials.

sentences.zh: 垂上言：

translations.literal: Chui submitted a memorial:
translations.idiomatic: Chui memorialized:

sentences.zh: 臣所至，並稱黃河水入王莽沙河與西河故瀆，注金、赤河，必慮水勢浩大，蕩浸民田，難於防備。

translations.literal: Everywhere I went, all said that if Yellow River water entered the Wang Mang Sha River and the old channel of the Western River, pouring into the Jin and Red rivers, they must fear the water's force would be vast, inundating the people's fields and proving hard to defend against.
translations.idiomatic: Everywhere I went officials warned that diverting the Yellow River into the Wang Mang Sha River and the Western River's old channel — and then into the Jin and Red rivers — would unleash such force as to inundate farmland beyond defense.

sentences.zh: 臣亦以為河水所經，不無為害。

translations.literal: Your subject also holds that wherever river water passes, harm is never absent.
translations.idiomatic: I agree that wherever the river runs, harm follows.

sentences.zh: 今者決河而南，為害既多，而又陽武埽東、石堰埽西，地形汙下，東河泄水又艱。

translations.literal: Now that the river has breached southward, the harm is already great; moreover, east of Yangwu bund and west of Shiyan bund the terrain is low and depressed, and discharging water eastward is again difficult.
translations.idiomatic: The southern breach has already done great harm. East of Yangwu bund and west of Shiyan bund the terrain is low-lying, and draining water eastward is difficult.

sentences.zh: 或者云：「今決處漕底坑深，舊渠逆上，若塞之，旁勞必復壞。

translations.literal: Some say: "At the present breach the canal bottom pit is deep and the old channel runs counter to the current; if it is blocked, the neighboring bunds will surely break again."
translations.idiomatic: Some argue: "The breach site has a deep pit and the old channel runs against the current. If we seal it, neighboring dikes will break again."

sentences.zh: 」如是，則議塞河者誠以為難。

translations.literal: Thus those who propose blocking the river truly find it difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Those who favor blocking the breach have a genuine case.

sentences.zh: 若決河而北，為害雖少，一旦河水注御河，蕩易水，逕乾寧軍，入獨流口，遂及契丹之境。

translations.literal: If the river breaches northward, the harm would be less — yet once river water pours into the Imperial Canal, surges through the Yi River, passes Ganning Army, enters Duliu mouth, and reaches Khitan territory.
translations.idiomatic: A northern breach would do less immediate harm — yet once the river poured into the Imperial Canal, surged through the Yi, passed Ganning Army and Duliu mouth, it would reach Khitan territory.

sentences.zh: 或者云：「因此搖動邊鄙。

translations.literal: Some say: "This would thereby shake the frontier."
translations.idiomatic: Others warn: "This would unsettle the frontier."

sentences.zh: 」如是，則議疏河者又益為難。

translations.literal: Thus those who propose dredging the river find their case even harder.
translations.idiomatic: Those who favor dredging face an even harder argument.

sentences.zh: 臣於兩難之間，輒畫一計：請自上流引北載之高地，東至大伾，瀉復於澶淵舊道，使南不至滑州，北不出通利軍界。

translations.literal: Between these two difficulties, your subject has drawn up one plan: request that from the upper reaches the river be drawn north onto high ground, east to Dapi, discharged back into the old channel of Chanyuan, so that south it does not reach Huazhou and north it does not exit the border of Tongli Army.
translations.idiomatic: Between these dilemmas I propose a third course: draw the river from upstream onto high ground northward, east to Dapi, and discharge it back into Chanyuan's old channel — so it neither reaches Huazhou to the south nor crosses Tongli Army's border to the north.

sentences.zh: 何以計之？

translations.literal: How is this to be planned?
translations.idiomatic: How would this work?

sentences.zh: 臣請自衛州東界曹公所開運渠東五里，河北岸凸處，就岸實土堅引之，正北稍東十三里，破伯禹古堤，注裴家潭，逕牧馬陂，又正東稍北四十里，鑿大伾西山，釃為二渠：一逼大伾南足，決古堤正東八里，復澶淵舊道；

translations.literal: Your subject requests that from Weizhou's eastern border, five li east of the transport canal opened by Lord Cao, at a projecting point on the north bank, earth be packed along the bank to draw the water due north and slightly east for thirteen li, breaking through the ancient dike of the Earl of Yu, pouring into Peijia Pool, passing the Horse-Pasturing Marsh, then due east and slightly north for forty li, cutting through the western mountain of Dapi and dividing into two channels: one pressing the southern foot of Dapi, breaching the ancient dike due east for eight li to restore the old channel of Chanyuan;
translations.idiomatic: From Weizhou's eastern border, five li east of Cao Cao's transport canal, pack earth along a projecting point on the north bank to draw the water due north and slightly east for thirteen li, break Yu's ancient dike, pour into Peijia Pool, pass the Horse-Pasturing Marsh, then forty li east and slightly north, cut through Dapi's western mountain, and divide into two channels: one along Dapi's southern foot, breaching the ancient dike eight li east to restore Chanyuan's old course;

sentences.zh: 一逼通利軍城北曲河口，至大禹所導西河故瀆，正北稍東五里，開南北大堤，又東七里，入澶淵舊道，與南渠合。

translations.literal: one pressing the curved river mouth north of Tongli Army city, reaching the old channel of the Western River guided by Great Yu, due north and slightly east for five li, opening great north-south dikes, then seven li east into the old channel of Chanyuan, joining the southern channel.
translations.idiomatic: one along the curved river mouth north of Tongli Army city to Yu's Western River old channel, five li due north and slightly east, opening great north-south dikes, then seven li east into Chanyuan's old course to join the southern channel.

sentences.zh: 夫如是，則北載之高地，大伾二山脽股之間分酌其勢，浚瀉兩渠，匯注東北，不遠三十里，復合於澶淵舊道，而滑州不治自涸矣。

translations.literal: If so, bearing the river on high ground northward, between the two foothills of Dapi its force would be divided and apportioned, the two channels dredged and discharged, gathering northeast — within thirty li rejoining the old channel of Chanyuan, and Huazhou without treatment would dry up of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Thus carried on high ground, the river's force would be split between Dapi's two foothills, channeled through two dredged outlets gathering northeast, rejoining Chanyuan's old course within thirty li — and Huazhou would dry up without further intervention.

sentences.zh: 臣請以兵夫二萬，自來歲二月興作，除三伏半功外，至十月而成。

translations.literal: Your subject requests twenty thousand soldiers and laborers, work to begin in the second month of the coming year, half effort during the three fu days of midsummer excepted, completed by the tenth month.
translations.idiomatic: I request twenty thousand soldiers and laborers, starting work in the second month of next year, half effort during midsummer's three fu periods, completion by the tenth month.

sentences.zh: 其均厚埤薄，俟次年可也。

translations.literal: As for leveling thick and thin, low and high — that may await the following year.
translations.idiomatic: Leveling high and low ground can wait until the following year.

sentences.zh: 疏奏，朝議慮其煩擾，罷之。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; court deliberation feared the burden and trouble, and the plan was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial reached court, but deliberation feared the burden and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 初，滑州以天臺決口去水稍遠，聊興葺之，及西南堤成，乃於天臺口旁築月堤。

translations.literal: Initially, because the Tiantai breach at Huazhou was somewhat distant from the water, repairs were undertaken casually; once the southwest dike was completed, a crescent dike was built beside the Tiantai mouth.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Huazhou made only casual repairs at the Tiantai breach, which lay somewhat away from the main current. Once the southwest dike was finished, a crescent-shaped dike was built beside the Tiantai mouth.

sentences.zh: 六月望，河復決天臺下，走衛南，浮徐、濟，害如三年而益甚，帝以新經賦率，慮殫困民力，即詔京東西、河北路經水災州軍，勿復科調丁夫，其守扞堤防役兵，仍令長吏存恤而番休之。

translations.literal: On the full moon of the sixth month, the river again breached below Tiantai, ran south through Wei, and floated across Xu and Ji — the harm like that of the third year but worse. The Emperor, having recently imposed tax levies, feared exhausting the people's strength and immediately ordered that in Jingdong, Jingxi, and Hebei circuits, prefectures and armies that had suffered flood disaster were not again to levy corvée laborers; for soldiers guarding the dikes, chief officials were still to show care and grant them rotation rest.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth month's full moon the river broke again below Tiantai, running south through Wei and flooding Xu and Ji — worse than three years before. With fresh tax levies just imposed, the Emperor feared exhausting the people and ordered flood-affected prefectures in Jingdong, Jingxi, and Hebei to levy no more conscript labor. Soldiers on dike duty were to receive care and rotating rest from their commanders.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，知滑州陳堯佐以西北水壞，城無外禦，築大堤，又疊埽於城北，護州中居民；

translations.literal: In the first month of the fifth year, Huazhou prefect Chen Yaozuo, because northwestern floodwaters had destroyed defenses and the city had no outer protection, built a great dike and also stacked bunds north of the city to shield the residents within the prefecture;
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fifth year Huazhou prefect Chen Yaozuo, with northwestern floods having destroyed outer defenses, built a great dike and stacked river bundles north of the city to protect residents;

sentences.zh: 復就鑿橫木，下垂木數條，置水旁以護岸，謂之「木龍」，當時賴焉。

translations.literal: he also had cross-timbers carved with several hanging wooden strips placed beside the water to protect the bank — called "wooden dragons" — on which the city relied at the time.
translations.idiomatic: he also had cross-timbers carved with hanging wooden strips placed along the bank to break the current — called "wooden dragons" — on which the city then relied.

sentences.zh: 復並舊河開枝流，以分導水勢，有詔嘉獎。

translations.literal: He also joined the old river in opening branch streams to divide and guide the water's force; an edict commended and rewarded him.
translations.idiomatic: He also opened branch channels from the old river to split the current. An edict commended his work.

sentences.zh: 說者以黃河隨時漲落，故舉物候為水勢之名：自立春之後，東風解凍，河邊入候水，初至凡一寸，則夏秋當至一尺，頗為信驗，故謂之「信水」。

translations.literal: Expositors, because the Yellow River rises and falls with the seasons, take natural signs as names for water conditions: after the Beginning of Spring, when east winds thaw the ice, river watchers observe the water — when it first reaches one inch, summer and autumn will see one foot; this is quite reliably verified, hence it is called "trustworthy water."
translations.idiomatic: Commentators note that the Yellow River rises and falls with the seasons and name each stage by natural signs. After the Beginning of Spring, when east winds thaw the ice, watchers record the first rise — one inch foretells a foot by summer and autumn. This sign has proved reliable, hence "trustworthy water."

sentences.zh: 二月、三月桃華始開，冰泮兩積，川流猥集，波瀾盛長，謂之「桃華水」。

translations.literal: In the second and third months peach blossoms first open, ice melts and snow accumulations release, streams gather in multitude, and waves swell greatly — this is called "peach-blossom water."
translations.idiomatic: In the second and third months, as peach blossoms open, ice and snowmelt release their waters and streams converge in swelling waves — "peach-blossom water."

sentences.zh: 春末蕪菁華開，謂之「菜華水」。

translations.literal: At late spring when turnip flowers open, it is called "vegetable-blossom water."
translations.idiomatic: When turnip flowers bloom in late spring — "vegetable-blossom water."

sentences.zh: 四月末壟麥結秀，擢芒變色，謂之「麥黃水」。

translations.literal: At the end of the fourth month ridge wheat forms ears and stalks change color — this is called "wheat-yellow water."
translations.idiomatic: At month's end in the fourth month, as wheat ears form and stalks turn golden — "wheat-yellow water."

sentences.zh: 五月瓜實延蔓，謂之「瓜蔓水」。

translations.literal: In the fifth month melons spread their vines — this is called "melon-vine water."
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, as melon vines spread — "melon-vine water."

sentences.zh: 朔野之地，深山窮谷，固陰冱寒，冰堅晚泮，逮乎盛夏，消釋方盡，而沃蕩山石，水帶礬腥，並流於河，故六月中旬後，謂之「礬山水」。

translations.literal: In the northern wilds, deep mountains and remote valleys hold enduring yin and penetrating cold; ice remains hard and melts late — not until midsummer is the melt complete. Waters that have washed over rocks carry alum's brackish taste and all flow into the river; hence after mid-sixth month it is called "alum-mountain water."
translations.idiomatic: In the northern wilds, ice in deep valleys melts only by midsummer. Waters washing over mineral-rich rocks carry alum's brackish tang into the river — after mid-sixth month, "alum-mountain water."

sentences.zh: 七月菽豆方秀，謂之「豆華水」。

translations.literal: In the seventh month beans and legumes are in flower — this is called "bean-blossom water."
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month, as beans flower — "bean-blossom water."

sentences.zh: 八月菼亂華，謂之「荻苗水」。

translations.literal: In the eighth month reeds and rushes bloom — this is called "reed-sprout water."
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month, as reeds bloom — "reed-sprout water."

sentences.zh: 九月以重陽紀節，謂之「登高水」。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, marked by the Double Yang festival, it is called "climbing-high water."
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month, around the Double Yang festival — "climbing-high water."

sentences.zh: 十月水落安流，復其故道，謂之「復槽水」。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the water falls and flows peacefully, returning to its old channel — this is called "returning-channel water."
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the waters subside and return to their channel — "returning-channel water."

sentences.zh: 十一月、十二月斷冰雜流，乘寒復結，謂之「蹙淩水」。

translations.literal: In the eleventh and twelfth months broken ice and mixed currents, taking advantage of cold, freeze again — this is called "compressed-ice water."
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh and twelfth months, as broken ice and mixed currents freeze again in the cold — "compressed-ice water."

sentences.zh: 水信有常，率以為准；

translations.literal: The water signs have regularity and are generally taken as standards;
translations.idiomatic: These seasonal signs follow regular patterns and serve as standards;

sentences.zh: 非時暴漲，謂之「客水」。

translations.literal: untimely violent rises are called "guest water."
translations.idiomatic: untimely violent floods are called "guest water."

sentences.zh: 其水勢，凡移谼橫注，岸如刺毀，謂之「紮岸」。

translations.literal: As for water conditions: whenever a channel shifts and pours crosswise, the bank pierced as if destroyed — this is called "piercing the bank."
translations.idiomatic: Among water conditions: when a channel shifts and pours crosswise, piercing the bank as if with stakes — "piercing the bank."

sentences.zh: 漲溢逾防，謂之「抹岸」。

translations.literal: Rising and overflowing beyond the defenses — this is called "smearing the bank."
translations.idiomatic: When floodwaters rise over the embankment — "smearing the bank."

sentences.zh: 埽岸故朽，潛流漱其下，謂之「塌岸」。

translations.literal: When a bund bank is old and rotten and hidden currents scour beneath — this is called "collapsing bank."
translations.idiomatic: When an old bundle-bank rots and hidden currents scour beneath — "collapsing bank."

sentences.zh: 浪勢旋激，岸土上隤，謂之「淪卷」。

translations.literal: When wave force swirls and drives, bank earth slides down from above — this is called "bank-collapse roll."
translations.idiomatic: When swirling waves undercut the bank from above — "bank-collapse roll."

sentences.zh: 水侵岸逆漲，謂之「上展」。

translations.literal: When water invades the bank and rises against the current — this is called "upstream spread."
translations.idiomatic: When water pushes up against the bank against the current — "upstream spread."

sentences.zh: 順漲，謂之「下展」。

translations.literal: Rising with the current — this is called "downstream spread."
translations.idiomatic: Rising with the current — "downstream spread."

sentences.zh: 或水乍落，直流之中，忽屈曲橫射，謂之「徑{穴叫}」。

translations.literal: Or when water suddenly drops, in the straight current it suddenly bends and shoots crosswise — this is called "direct cross-burst."
translations.idiomatic: Or when water suddenly falls, a straight current abruptly bends and shoots sideways — "direct cross-burst."

sentences.zh: 水猛驟移，其將澄處，望之明白，謂之「拽白」，亦謂之「明灘」。

translations.literal: When water shifts violently and suddenly, where it is about to clear, viewed from afar it appears bright — this is called "dragging white," also called "bright shoal."
translations.idiomatic: When violent currents shift suddenly, the approaching clear stretch looks bright from afar — "dragging white," also "bright shoal."

sentences.zh: 湍怒略渟，勢稍汩起，行舟值之多溺，謂之「薦浪水」。

translations.literal: When rapids rage and briefly pause, the force slightly wells up — boats that encounter it often sink — this is called "recommending-wave water."
translations.idiomatic: When raging rapids briefly pause and swell upward, boats that hit them often sink — "standing-wave water."

sentences.zh: 水退淤澱，夏則膠土肥腴。

translations.literal: When water retreats it deposits silt; in summer this becomes glutinous, fertile soil.
translations.idiomatic: When the waters recede they leave silt; in summer this becomes rich, glutinous soil.

sentences.zh: 初秋則黃滅土，頗為疏壤，深秋則白滅土，霜降後皆沙也。

translations.literal: In early autumn it becomes yellow depleted soil, rather loose in texture; in late autumn it becomes white depleted soil — after Frost's Descent all is sand.
translations.idiomatic: Early autumn deposits yield yellow, somewhat loose soil; late autumn yields white depleted soil — after Frost's Descent it is all sand.

sentences.zh: 舊制，歲虞河決，有司常以孟秋預調塞治之物，梢芟、薪柴、楗橛、竹石、茭索、竹索凡千余萬，謂之「春料」。

translations.literal: By old regulation, fearing river breaches each year, officials regularly in mid-autumn pre-levied materials for blocking and repair — tips, reeds, fuel, piles, bamboo, stone, rush rope, and bamboo rope totaling more than ten million units — called "spring stock."
translations.idiomatic: By regulation, officials each mid-autumn pre-levied flood-repair materials — brush, reeds, timber, piles, bamboo, stone, rush rope, and bamboo rope totaling over ten million units — called "spring stock."

sentences.zh: 詔下瀕河諸州所產之地，仍遣使會河渠官吏，乘農隙率丁夫水工，收采備用。

translations.literal: Edicts were sent to the producing regions of riverine prefectures; envoys still convened river officials, and during agricultural slack seasons led corvée laborers and water workers to gather and store materials for use.
translations.idiomatic: Edicts went to riverine prefectures' producing regions. Envoys convened river officials and, during agricultural slack seasons, led laborers and water workers to gather and stock materials.

sentences.zh: 凡伐蘆荻謂之「芟」，伐山木榆柳枝葉謂之「梢」，辮竹糾芟為索。

translations.literal: Cutting reeds and rushes was called "jian"; cutting mountain trees' elm and willow branches and leaves was called "shao"; plaiting bamboo and binding jian into rope.
translations.idiomatic: Cutting reeds and rushes was called jian; cutting elm and willow branches was called shao; plaiting bamboo and binding jian into rope.

sentences.zh: 以竹為巨索，長十尺至百尺，有數等。

translations.literal: Bamboo was made into great ropes from ten to one hundred feet in length, in several grades.
translations.idiomatic: Bamboo was fashioned into great ropes ten to one hundred feet long, in several grades.

sentences.zh: 先擇寬平之所為埽場。

translations.literal: First a broad, level place was chosen as the bund yard.
translations.idiomatic: First a broad, level site was chosen as the bund yard.

sentences.zh: 埽之制，密佈芟索，鋪梢，梢芟相重，壓之以土，雜以碎石，以巨竹索橫貫其中，謂之「心索」。

translations.literal: The bund's construction: jian and rope densely laid, shao spread, shao and jian layered upon each other, pressed with earth mixed with broken stone, a great bamboo rope run crosswise through the middle — called the "heart rope."
translations.idiomatic: A bund was built by densely layering jian and rope, spreading shao atop, alternating layers, pressing with earth and broken stone, and running a great bamboo rope crosswise through the center — the "heart rope."

sentences.zh: 卷而束之，復以大芟索擊其兩端，別以竹索自內旁出，其高至數丈，其長倍之。

translations.literal: It was rolled and bound; great jian ropes again struck its two ends; separate bamboo ropes issued from within at the sides — its height reaching several zhang, its length double that.
translations.idiomatic: The mass was rolled and bound, great jian ropes lashed to both ends, bamboo ropes issuing from the sides — several zhang high and twice as long.

sentences.zh: 凡用丁夫數百或千人，雜唱齊挽，積置於卑薄之處，謂之「埽岸」。

translations.literal: Several hundred or a thousand laborers were used, singing in chorus as they hauled together, stacking them at low, thin places — called "bund bank."
translations.idiomatic: Hundreds or a thousand laborers hauled in chorus and stacked the bundles at weak points in the bank — "bund bank."

sentences.zh: 既下，以橛臬閡之，復以長木貫之，其竹索皆埋巨木於岸以維之，遇河之橫決，則復增之，以補其缺。

translations.literal: Once lowered, piles and stakes blocked it; long timbers were again run through; the bamboo ropes all had great timbers buried in the bank to secure them. When the river breached crosswise, more were added to fill the gap.
translations.idiomatic: Once placed, piles and stakes held them in place and long timbers were driven through. Bamboo ropes were anchored to great timbers buried in the bank. When the river breached, more bundles were added to fill gaps.

sentences.zh: 凡埽下非積數疊，亦不能遏其迅湍，又有馬頭、鋸牙、木岸者，以蹙水勢護堤焉。

translations.literal: Unless several layers were stacked below a bund, swift rapids could not be checked; there were also horse-head, saw-tooth, and wooden-bank structures to compress the water's force and protect the dikes.
translations.idiomatic: Without multiple stacked layers a single bund could not check swift currents. Horse-head, saw-tooth, and wooden-bank structures also compressed the current to protect the dikes.

sentences.zh: 凡緣河諸州，孟州有河南北凡二埽，開封府有陽武埽，滑州有韓房二村、憑管、石堰、州西、魚池、迎陽凡七埽，舊有七里曲埽，後廢。

translations.literal: Among all riverine prefectures: Mengzhou had two bunds south and north of the river; Kaifeng prefecture had Yangwu bund; Huazhou had Han and Fang two villages, Pingguan, Shiyan, west of the prefecture, Yuchi, and Yingyang — seven bunds in all; formerly there was Qiliqu bund, later abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Along the river: Mengzhou had two bunds north and south of the channel; Kaifeng had Yangwu bund; Huazhou had seven — at Han and Fang villages, Pingguan, Shiyan, west of the city, Yuchi, and Yingyang (the old Qiliqu bund was later abandoned).

sentences.zh: 通利軍有齊賈、蘇村凡二埽，澶州有濮陽、大韓、大吳、商胡、王楚、橫隴、曹村、依仁、大北、岡孫、陳固、明公、王八凡十三埽，大名府有孫杜、侯村二埽，濮州有任村、東、西、北凡四埽，鄆州有博陵、張秋、關山、子路、王陵、竹口凡六埽，齊州有採金山、史家渦二埽，濱州有平河、安定二埽，棣州有聶家、梭堤、鋸牙、陽成四埽，所費皆有司歲計而無闕焉。

translations.literal: Tongli Army had Qijia and Sucun — two bunds; Chanzhou had Puyang, Dahan, Dawu, Shanghu, Wangchu, Henglong, Caocun, Yiren, Dabei, Gangsun, Chengu, Minggong, and Wangba — thirteen bunds; Daming prefecture had Sundu and Houcun — two bunds; Puzhou had Rencun, east, west, and north — four bunds; Yunzhou had Boling, Zhangqiu, Guanshan, Zilu, Wangling, and Zhukou — six bunds; Qizhou had Caijinshan and Shijiawo — two bunds; Binzhou had Pinghe and Anding — two bunds; Dizhou had Nieji, Suodi, Juya, and Yangcheng — four bunds. Expenses for all were annually calculated by officials without shortfall.
translations.idiomatic: Tongli Army had two bunds (Qijia, Sucun); Chanzhou thirteen (Puyang, Dahan, Dawu, Shanghu, Wangchu, Henglong, Caocun, Yiren, Dabei, Gangsun, Chengu, Minggong, Wangba); Daming two (Sundu, Houcun); Puzhou four (Rencun and east, west, north); Yunzhou six (Boling, Zhangqiu, Guanshan, Zilu, Wangling, Zhukou); Qizhou two (Caijinshan, Shijiawo); Binzhou two (Pinghe, Anding); Dizhou four (Nieji, Suodi, Juya, Yangcheng). Officials budgeted for all annually without shortfall.

sentences.zh: 六年八月，河決於澶州之王楚埽，凡三十步。
